drivingQuestion: From where is it derived that the shekel-contribution year begins in Nisan?
outcomeNote: The source is given; the next unit tests the gezera shava.

segments.he: וְלִתְרוּמַת שְׁקָלִים. מְנָלַן? אָמַר רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה, אָמַר קְרָא: ״זֹאת עוֹלַת חֹדֶשׁ בְּחׇדְשׁוֹ לְחׇדְשֵׁי הַשָּׁנָה״ — אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה: חַדֵּשׁ וְהָבֵא קׇרְבָּן מִתְּרוּמָה חֲדָשָׁה. וְגָמְרִי ״שָׁנָה״ ״שָׁנָה״ מִנִּיסָן, דִּכְתִיב: ״רִאשׁוֹן הוּא לָכֶם לְחׇדְשֵׁי הַשָּׁנָה״.
segments.en: § It was taught in the baraita: «And» the first of Nisan is the New Year «for collection of» the «shekels» that had been collected in Adar and were used to purchase animals for communal offerings and other needs of the Temple. The Gemara asks: «From where do we» derive this? «Rabbi Yoshiya said» that «the verse states: “This is the burnt-offering of each month in its month throughout the months [leḥodshei] of the year”» (Numbers 28:14). The seemingly superfluous term: “Throughout the months [leḥodshei] of the year,” should be understood as follows: «The Torah is saying» here: «Renew [ḥaddesh]» the year «and bring an offering from the new collection» of the shekels. «And it is derived» by way of a verbal analogy between one instance of the word «“year”» and another instance of the word «“year”» that the year begins for this purpose «from Nisan, as it is written» with regard to Nisan: «“It shall be the first month of the year to you”» (Exodus 12:2).
